'''Ibrahim Haddad''' ({{langx|ar|ابراهيم حداد}}) (born 1938) is a Syrian politician who served as minister of oil and mineral reserves from December 2001 to February 2006.

==Early life and education==
Haddad was born into a Christian family in Ain Ghara Tal Kalakh, [[Homs Governorate]], in 1938.<ref name=freeall/><ref name=silo09>{{cite news|title=Biography for Ibrahim Haddad|url=http://news.silobreaker.com/biography-for-ibrahim-haddad-5_2256865734573424640_4|access-date=24 February 2013|work=Silobreaker|date=15 January 2009|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411193436/http://news.silobreaker.com/biography-for-ibrahim-haddad-5_2256865734573424640_4#|archive-date=11 April 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> He holds a PhD in [[radiation physics]], which he received from [[the University of Reading]] in 1966.<ref name=silo09/>

==Career==
Haddad served as the director general of Syria's Atomic Energy Commission until 2001.<ref name=freeall>{{cite news|title=Sufian 'Allaw
|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/SYRIA+-+Sufian+'Allaw.-a0223297959|access-date=24 February 2013|work=APS Review Oil Market Trends|date=29 March 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=List of Participants|url=http://www.iaea.org/About/Policy/GC/GC30/GC30InfDocuments/English/gc30inf-238_en.pdf|publisher=International Atomic Energy Agency|access-date=24 February 2013|date=19 September 1986}}</ref> He was also Syria's delegate to the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]].<ref>{{cite news|title=New Syrian Government Formed; Veteran Guards Retain Defence and Foreign Portfolios|url=http://www.albawaba.com/news/new-syrian-government-formed-veteran-guards-retain-defence-and-foreign-portfolios|access-date=24 February 2013|work=[[Al Bawaba]]|date=14 December 2001}}</ref>

He was appointed oil minister on 13 December 2001, replacing [[Maher Jamal]] in the post.<ref name=apsdip31>{{cite news|title=Profile – Dr. Ibrahim Haddad|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/SYRIA+-+Profile+-+Dr.+Ibrahim+Haddad.-a099556737|access-date=12 March 2013|work=APS Diplomat Operations in Oil Diplomacy|date=31 March 2003}}</ref> He was an independent member of [[Cabinet of Syria (2001–2003)|the cabinet]] headed by Prime Minister [[Muhammad Mustafa Mero|Mohammad Mustafa Mero]]. Haddad continued to serve in the same post in [[Cabinet of Syria (2003–2011)|the cabinet]] led by Prime Minister [[Muhammad Naji al-Otari|Mohammad Naji Al Otari]], which was formed in 2003. Haddad's term lasted until 11 February 2006, and was replaced by [[Sufian Allaw]] as oil minister.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Sami Moubayed|title=Strengthening the line
|journal=Al-Ahram Weekly|date=16–22 February 2006|url=http://weekly.ahram.org.eg/2006/782/re302.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121224084300/http://weekly.ahram.org.eg/2006/782/re302.htm |archive-date=24 December 2012}}</ref>

After leaving office Haddad was appointed energy advisor to Otari in March 2006.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Former Syrian Oil Minister Appointed Government Advisor|url=https://archives.mees.com/issues/297/articles/12111|journal=Middle East Economic Survey|date=20 March 2006|volume=49
|issue=12}}</ref>

===Activities===
When Haddad was oil minister, Syria's oil production significantly declined to below 400,000 barrels/day (b/d) from a peak of 600,000 b/d in the mid-1990s.<ref>{{cite news|title=Syria politics: Assad tinkers|url=http://viewswire.eiu.com/index.asp?layout=VWArticleVW3&article_id=2009969386&country_id=30000003&channel_id=210004021&category_id=500004050&refm=vwCat&page_title=Article|access-date=24 February 2013|newspaper=[[The Economist]]|date=14 February 2006}}</ref> In addition, the Russian oil company, [[Tatneft]], developed a contract with Syria to extract oil in the country during his term in March 2005.<ref name=meria>{{cite journal|author=Mark N. Katz|title=Putin's Foreign Policy Toward Syria|journal=MERIA|year=2006|url=http://ebot.gmu.edu/bitstream/handle/1920/3024/Putin%20Syria%20MERIA.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y}}</ref> It was the first oil contract between Syria and [[Russia]].<ref name=meria/>
